evidence.excerpt: A method is described for identifying deviating fermentation batches in real time by calculating a set of seven metabolite ratios from spent broth samples collected at defined process time points and comparing these ratios against control limits established from historical reference batches. The method applies to submerged bacterial fermentation processes producing extracellular enzymes or organic acids. It requires a single LC-MS analysis per time-point sample and produces a scalar deviation index that can trigger process intervention or batch rejection decisions without operator expertise in metabolomics data interpretation.
